samples.summary: Decimal step on a column/row/whole-sheet selection turns a previously O(1) layer write into a full-document scan with an uncached `Intl.NumberFormat` construction per currency cell — a main-thread stall proportional to document size, triggered by one button press
samples.evidence: Before this change, `setRangeStyle` for `selectionType` 'column'/'row'/'all' never touched cells at all (sheet.ts:3739-3784). `changeDecimals` now calls `selectionRendersAt` (sheet.ts:4374) and `unsetKeepsRendering` (sheet.ts:4414), which both do `await this.store.getGrid(range)` over `selectionTargets()`; for `selectAllCells()` that range is the whole `dimensionRange` (sheet.ts:3015), so the scan covers every populated cell in the document. For each such cell `selectionRendersAt` calls `renderedDecimals` (sheet.ts:4386), which for a `dp`-less currency cell constructs a fresh `new Intl.NumberFormat(...)` per cell with no cache (format.ts:151); `unsetKeepsRendering` calls `formatValue` twice per cell (sheet.ts:4434-4435), each of which constructs Intl formatters via `toLocaleString`. `unsetRangeStyleValues` then adds an `await this.store.get(anchor)` per cell (sheet.ts:4554). Attack: any collaborator (or an `.xlsx` import) grows the shared document to a large populated cell count and gives cells `nf: 'currency'`; a victim who selects-all and presses Decrease Decimals blocks the renderer for a duration the attacker controls via document size. All `getGrid` implementations are index-based (memory.ts:145, yorkie-store.ts:445), so the cost is linear in populated cells rather than in the 1,000,000 x 18,278 dimension range — which bounds the impact to a freeze rather than a hang, hence minor.

samples.summary: `collectStyleValuesToPin` writes a caller-supplied key name into a plain object via a computed property assignment, a prototype-pollution-shaped sink reachable from the newly public `setRangeStyle(style, { defaultKeys })` option
samples.evidence: `setRangeStyle` gained a public `options.defaultKeys` parameter (sheet.ts:3732-3735) whose values flow unchecked into `collectStyleValuesToPin`, where they are used as a dynamic key in `(keep as Record<string, unknown>)[key] = value;` (sheet.ts:3843). `keep` is an object literal with `Object.prototype`, so a `key` of `'__proto__'` invokes the prototype setter rather than defining an own property, and `'constructor'`/`'prototype'` chains are likewise unfiltered. I could not complete the exploit chain: the only in-repo caller passes the literal `['nf']` (sheet.ts:4359); the TypeScript signature is `Array<keyof CellStyle>`, which is compile-time only; and for `key === '__proto__'` the guard `value === patch[key]` at sheet.ts:3840 would compare `Object.prototype` to `Object.prototype` and skip the write for a plain-object patch. So this is a latent sink, not a demonstrated vector — hence low confidence. Hardening: build `keep` with `Object.create(null)` or reject keys not in an allowlist of `CellStyle` keys before assigning.

samples.summary: The new `defaultKeys` pinning path materialises a per-cell style write for every populated cell in the selection, amplifying an O(1) layer-level format into O(N) entries in the shared persisted document
samples.evidence: `setRangeStyle` now iterates the map returned by `collectStyleValuesToPin` and issues `await this.setStyle(parseRef(sref), keep)` per cell (sheet.ts:3802-3804), and `changeDecimals` reaches this path on every step whose active cell has a plain/absent format (`setRangeStyle(patch, { defaultKeys: ['nf'] })`, sheet.ts:4359). When the selection inherits a format from a column/row/sheet layer, each populated cell in it gains its own `cell.s.nf`. An editor pressing Decrease once over a large multi-cell selection therefore converts a single stored layer style into one persisted style object per cell in the collaborative CRDT document, growing server-side storage and sync traffic by a factor proportional to the selection's populated cell count. This is write amplification available to any authorised editor, not an authorisation break, so impact is bounded to resource consumption.

samples.summary: `unsetRangeStyleValues` is a new public model-level mutation with no write gate of its own; enforcement lives solely in the view layer, so any future caller that holds a `Sheet` bypasses read-only mode
samples.evidence: `unsetRangeStyleValues` (sheet.ts:4472) writes `store.setSheetStyle`/`setColumnStyle`/`setRowStyle`/`setRangeStyles`/`set`/`delete` and also mutates the in-memory `this.sheetStyle`/`colStyles`/`rowStyles`/`rangeStyles` directly (sheet.ts:4579, 4591, 4604, 4627). `Sheet` carries no read-only concept; the only gate is `if (!this.sheet || this._readOnly) return;` in the view (spreadsheet.ts:535, :545). I enumerated the call sites and found no bypass today: `changeDecimals`/`unsetRangeStyleValues` are called only from `spreadsheet.ts:536/546` and `sheet.ts:4346`, and the UI entry points are `formatting-toolbar.tsx:249/253`, all behind the guard. Note also that with a `ReadOnlyStore` the store writes are no-ops (readonly.ts:81, 204, 212, 220, 232) but the in-memory layer maps would still be mutated, leaving a divergent client view — unreachable today because the view gate fires first. Reported as a defence-in-depth observation only; it matches the pre-existing pattern for `setRangeStyle` and is not a regression.
